title: Run the romanx test-first pipeline: kill mutants, implement the full module, ship the CLI
goal: A test-first three-stage campaign. Stage 1 inverts the usual order: before writing any implementation, author a behavioral kill-test suite for the sealed romanx reference that stays green on the original and fails on at least 10 of its 12 sealed mutants (strict canonical-form validation hides the subtle ones). Stage 2 implements the full module - same core contract plus is_valid and an eagerly-validating roman_range generator - against a sealed suite. Stage 3 ships a CLI with pinned exit codes and stderr prefixes, graded by a sealed subprocess suite while stage 2 stays green. Plan freezing, a sha256 marker chain, a run journal, and an honest cost record are graded with final state as one campaign_score.
resources: pypi pytest==8.3.4 (installed by the sealed grader inside the container)
assets/gc-414/SPEC.md (reference contract, CLI contract, artifact contract)
process_expectations: The frozen plan restates the strict-canonical grammar and enumerates the mutant-facing behavior classes BEFORE stage 1 kill tests are written.
Kill tests are behavioral only (the grader bans source-introspection tokens and shadow copies) and reach the 10/12 threshold with a green baseline.
runs.log journals kill counts across stage-1 iterations and suite results for stages 2-3 with honest passed/failed integers.
The CLI stage does not regress the module stage: the grader re-runs the stage-2 suite after the CLI suite.
cost.json carries honest llm_usd and grader_runs totals for the campaign.
